title: Democrats Win Control of Congress as Voters Reject Trump's Party; Several Races Still Uncalled
dek: AP race calls give Democrats the Senate and control of both chambers, with flips in Kansas, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. Trump has said he will accept the results.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: NPR, based on AP race calls, reported Democrats have cemented control of both chambers of Congress, the first full Democratic control since 2023.
AP reported Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats: Kansas, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. They held Georgia and Michigan.
AP called Montana for Republican Kurt Alme at 2:54 a.m. EST and Nebraska for Republican Gov. Jim Pillen at 2:53 a.m. EST.
AP reported Democrats flipped more than two dozen House districts, some that Trump carried by double digits in 2024. This story does not give a final House seat total.
Trump told Fox News that he would accept the results and said part of the defeat was due to the Iran war.
body:
Democrats won control of Congress on Tuesday night, according to Associated Press race calls, reported by NPR and the AP. The results give Democrats the Senate and the House, ending Republican control of both chambers and setting up investigations into the Trump administration when the new Congress convenes in January.

## Senate

The Associated Press reported that Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats held by Republicans: Kansas, Iowa, Texas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. In Kansas, Adam Hamilton defeated Sen. Roger Marshall, the state's first Democratic senator since 1932, according to AP. In Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson defeated Sen. Susan Collins. Democrats also held Georgia, where Sen. Jon Ossoff won reelection, and Michigan, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers for an open seat. If confirmed, El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the Senate, according to AP and The Washington Post. Senate Democrats are expected to choose Chuck Schumer as majority leader when they hold leadership elections in early December, according to The Hill; Schumer said the results were a "generational remake of the Senate map."

Republicans held some races. The AP called Montana for Republican Kurt Alme, who defeated independent Seth Bodnar and Democrat Alani Bankhead, at 2:54 a.m. EST. Before the election, Republicans held a 53-47 Senate majority.

## House

AP reported that Democrats flipped more than two dozen House districts, some of which Trump won by double digits in 2024. NPR reported that Democrats flipped at least three Florida districts that the state's Republican legislature had redrawn, and ousted four Republican incumbents in competitive Pennsylvania districts. In Ohio's 9th District, AP called the race for Democratic Rep. Marcy Kaptur.

AP reported Wednesday morning that Democrats were closing in on a House majority, and NYT live coverage said Democrats were on track for at least a 50-seat majority. Meridian has not confirmed a final House seat total from AP, NBC or NYT, so this story does not give one.

## Trump's reaction

AP reported that Trump posted on social media before polls closed on the West Coast, blaming others for the losses, and shared an image of a red "veto" cap, signaling he would veto Democratic-controlled legislation. In a Fox News phone interview, he said he would accept the results. CBS News reported that Trump congratulated Democrats in a phone call with the network, while also threatening to use his "total veto power." The AP's results pages list the current tally and any races that remain uncalled. Meridian has not confirmed which individual House races are still uncalled.

## Governors

AP reported that Democrats flipped governors' offices in Georgia (Keisha Lance Bottoms), Ohio (Amy Acton), Iowa (Rob Sand) and Texas (Gina Hinojosa). AP called Nebraska for Republican Gov. Jim Pillen at 2:53 a.m. EST.

## Reaction

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, a Republican, said on X that Senate Republicans "will not stand idly by." House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Democrats would act on "transformational change" when they take office. Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., expected to chair the House Oversight Committee, posted on X: "LAWYER UP."

Trump posted on social media before polls closed on the West Coast that he was not on the ballot. In a late-night phone interview with Fox News, he said he would accept the results and that voters "didn't like the candidates." He also said he had been hurt by rising fuel prices and that the Iran war played a part in the losses. Trump has also said he would veto Democratic-passed legislation.

The results mean legislation will need Trump's signature to become law, and Democrats will need Republican votes for must-pass items, including the 12 annual appropriations bills.

## What is still open

The AP's live coverage described the results as a broad Democratic win. Meridian will update this story when the AP calls additional House races or if any recount or legal action changes a called result.
